TimelineJS 3 (MPL-2.0), vendored from KnightLab's CDN.

  js/timeline-min.js      https://cdn.knightlab.com/libs/timeline3/latest/js/timeline-min.js
  css/timeline.css        https://cdn.knightlab.com/libs/timeline3/latest/css/timeline.css
  css/icons/tl-icons.*    https://cdn.knightlab.com/libs/timeline3/latest/css/icons/
  css/fonts/font.default.css
                          https://cdn.knightlab.com/libs/timeline3/latest/css/fonts/font.default.css

Fetched 2026-08-20. The home page used to load all of this from that CDN, with
a Google Sheet id in the query string; see ../../timeline/ for what replaced
that arrangement and ../../timeline/media/PROVENANCE.txt for the slide images.

FOUR CHANGES TO WHAT THE CDN SERVED
-----------------------------------

1. css/fonts/font.default.css pointed at four PT Sans / PT Serif / PT Sans
   Narrow faces on fonts.gstatic.com. Those are in css/fonts/files/ now and the
   stylesheet names them locally.

2. css/timeline.css declared the tl-icons face in five formats. It is trimmed
   to woff2 + woff, and the .eot, .ttf and .svg files are not kept; they only
   ever served IE8 and Android 4.

3. Three of KnightLab's own API credentials are redacted from
   js/timeline-min.js. They ship in the public CDN bundle, so they are not
   secret in any meaningful sense, but they are not ours to publish and
   GitHub's secret scanning is right to object to them sitting in a repository:

     api_key_flickr:"bd3a7c45ddd52f3101825d41563a6125"      -> ""
     api_key_googlemaps:"AIzaSyB9dW8e_iRrATFa8g24qB6BDBGdkrLDZYI"  -> ""
     instagram_oembed?access_token=704270473831239|830b2107...  -> access_token=

   The third is a Facebook app access token in appid|appsecret form, used by
   the Instagram oEmbed media handler.

   Nothing in this archive can reach any of the three. All 20 media and
   background URLs in ../../timeline/timeline.json are local files -- twelve
   under /files/ in the object bucket and eight mirrored in
   ../../timeline/media/ -- so the Flickr, Google Maps and Instagram media
   handlers are never constructed. If a Flickr or Instagram slide were ever
   added to timeline.json it would now fail to load rather than quietly spend
   somebody else's quota, which is the behaviour an archive should have.

   The redaction is three string literals; the bundle is otherwise byte-for-byte
   what the CDN served, and it still parses and runs.

4. Nothing else. In particular the library's other third-party endpoints
   (Vimeo, YouTube, SoundCloud, Wikipedia, DocumentCloud, Twitter, Bluesky) are
   left alone: they need no credentials, and none of them is reachable from
   this timeline's content either.

REFRESHING
----------
Re-fetching from the CDN will reinstate all four. Re-apply them, then confirm
the timeline still draws 20 slides -- one title and 19 events, 1877 to 1926.
